summary: Describes a way for hosts and gateways to send statistics data on request to a monitoring center or debugging host. Machines that wanted a remote statistics monitoring facility could implement it. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: Imagine a gauge on a machine that you can ask from far away: "How are you doing?" This protocol is how it answers with its numbers.

questions: what is the statistics server protocol
how to monitor hosts statistics remotely
subtitle: A lightweight protocol to retrieve statistics data from remote hosts and gateways over the network.

tldr.problem: Monitoring systems need a simple way to collect statistics like packet counts and error rates from distant hosts without the overhead of remote login or file transfer.
tldr.mechanism: STATSRV is a stateless service that listens for ASCII commands on port 133 (TCP or UDP) and responds with statistics data formatted for display.
tldr.outcome: Operators can monitor multiple hosts from a central location with minimal network overhead, but the protocol has no authentication and is not suitable for detailed machine analysis.

today: RFC 996 is Historic. It was intended for casual monitoring on trusted networks but has been superseded by modern management protocols like SNMP (RFC 1157) and other structured monitoring frameworks.

sections.title: The Need for Remote Statistics
sections.content: Many hosts and gateways keep statistics about network traffic, errors, and events. System administrators want to monitor these statistics on distant machines from a central location. Conventional methods like remote login or file transfer are intrusive if conducted frequently and require substantial modification to existing systems. STATSRV provides a lightweight alternative designed for casual monitoring and debugging.
sections.eli5: A system administrator wants to check how machines are doing without logging in or copying files. A quick statistics query is less disruptive.

sections.title: How STATSRV Works
sections.content: A STATSRV server listens on port 133 for client commands. A client sends a null-terminated ASCII command string, and the server responds with a null-terminated ASCII response suitable for display on a terminal or printer. The protocol can work over either TCP or UDP, though UDP is less intrusive. Responses must fit in a single 576-octet IP datagram if UDP is used. No special authentication is provided; the protocol is designed for use on trusted networks.
sections.eli5: You send the machine a command like a question, and it sends back an answer that looks like information on a computer screen.

sections.title: Use Cases and Limitations
sections.content: STATSRV is intended for exploratory development and ad-hoc monitoring, not as a full-function monitoring protocol for detailed reports. The Fuzzball system used it to display billboards for each network device, showing packet counts, errors, and status. Unix programs and shell scripts could query selected hosts on a periodic basis to build a simple monitoring facility. However, the lack of access control means that any host on the network can query statistics.
sections.eli5: This works well for a group of trusted computers checking on each other, but it is not secure enough for the public Internet.
